solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Firm heading for receivership and bankrupt, nothing to invest

indicators.note: to invest here is to put something inside, so the zero goes into the other letters
the heading of a word is its first letter, so take the start of receivership

parts.note: bankrupt means bust, as in a firm going bust
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A company on the brink of receivership, broke, with no money to put into the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company in the surface, but it is the adjective being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something strong, sturdy and not easily shaken or broken.

clue.text: After unexpected rise, double remaining

indicators.note: an unexpected rise comes out in a jumbled order

parts.note: dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: After a surprise increase, a doubling is still to come.
explanation.walkthrough: RISE, made 'unexpected', gives RESI.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over after the rest is gone, such as leftover liquid or a lingering effect.

clue.text: Bread rose, might you say?

definitions.meaning: a large loaf with a rounded, slashed top
a rose is a flower that blooms, so might jokingly be called something that blooms

explanation.surface: A baker asks whether the bread has risen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the past tense of rise, as dough does, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This loaf name also reads as a playful name for any flowering plant.

clue.text: Deny tears flowing, as hardly moving

indicators.note: the letters run freely into a new order, like flowing tears

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to cry, sitting still.
explanation.definitionFit: A seated, inactive way of life involves very little physical exertion.

clue.text: Sides batting intermittently

definitions.meaning: in cricket the field is split into the off side and the on side from the batsman's view, so these are the two sides for the one batting
now and then, on an irregular basis

explanation.surface: A report of cricket teams batting in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the off side and the on (leg) side are the two halves of the field as seen by the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something happening in bursts with gaps, now and again.

clue.text: Archer speedy with bar and lock

parts.note: flying means very fast
but and bar both mean except
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A fast-moving bowman with a weapon and a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archer' looks like a bowman, but means something that arches.
explanation.definitionFit: This external support on Gothic churches takes the form of an arch, so jokingly it is something that arches.

clue.text: A quarrel? That's about right?

indicators.note: the phrase says the first part goes around the right letter

parts.note: a row is a heated quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether an argument is the right description.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarrel is also a crossbow bolt, so the whole clue defines the answer as well as building it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is an old name for the square-headed bolt fired from a crossbow, a kind of missile.

clue.text: Bath time — time flies!

parts.note: a dip is a quick bathe
an era is a period of time
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: It is bath time, and time flies by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like a verb in 'time flies', but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the scientific order of two-winged insects, the true flies such as houseflies and gnats.

clue.text: Spice in upended stone cask

indicators.note: upended means turned on its end, so in a down entry the letters run upwards

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: Spice stored in a cask turned on its end.
explanation.walkthrough: GEMTUN read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of an evergreen tree, grated as a flavouring in cooking.

clue.text: Lifting equipment requiring defensive actions

definitions.meaning: a pulley system with rope used for hoisting heavy loads
in sport, a block and a tackle are both moves made by defenders

explanation.surface: Heavy hoisting gear that calls for protective measures.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a pulley hoist and also two defensive moves in sports such as football.

clue.text: Small joy of the cryptic crossword, a dangerous game?

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the clever manipulation of words is what solvers enjoy in cryptic puzzles

explanation.surface: A little pleasure of solving cryptics, which might be risky to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing with blades is a sport, a game of sorts, and one that carries obvious physical danger.

clue.text: After putting back, soak plant again

indicators.note: putting back means the word for the drinker is written in reverse order

parts.note: a soak is a heavy drinker, a toper

explanation.surface: Instructions for watering a plant: put it back, soak it, then plant it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' looks like a verb about watering, but it is a noun for a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: To move a houseplant into a fresh container is a gardening verb for transplanting it once more.

clue.text: Evil daughter has come in sozzled

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A disgraceful daughter has come home drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of COME IN, scrambled because 'sozzled', give EMONIC after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fiendish or devilish is wicked in the way a fiend from hell is.

clue.text: A couple of presents unlikely to be found?

definitions.meaning: two words meaning present, in time and in place: now, and here
in no place at all, so not going to turn up

explanation.surface: Two gifts that are hard to track down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like gifts, but means the present moment and the present place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something located in no place whatsoever cannot be discovered, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Choice of parts in rear half of boat: a large vessel

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the choice word goes into the middle of the other letters
the back two of the four letters of boat

parts.note: or is the word that offers a choice between alternatives

explanation.surface: A description of the stern section of a boat, with a big vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: AT, the back half of 'boat', plus A gives ATA, which OR 'parts'.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery leaving the heart is the body's largest blood vessel.

clue.text: Arrest essential to fix a contrary European

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the whole string is read backwards
essential to means at the heart of, so the arrest word sits inside the fix word

parts.note: to fix something is to nail it
to nab is to catch or arrest

explanation.surface: An awkward European person says that an arrest is needed to sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' looks like a description of the European, but it reverses NAINABLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Albania, a Balkan country, is a European by nationality.

clue.text: Musical success for me

definitions.meaning: a record at the top of the charts
an informal way of referring to oneself, as in looking after yourself first

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that a musical hit was a success for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart-topping single, and also the idiom for oneself as one's top priority.

clue.text: Game where good lord overcome by spirits

indicators.note: in a down entry the exclamation sits under the spirits

parts.note: gin and rum are two spirits
my! and good lord! are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A game in which a fine nobleman is overwhelmed by drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good lord' looks like a nobleman but is an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game for two in which players form sets and sequences, a variety of rummy.

clue.text: Company having typed badly, one filed work as a journalist

indicators.note: filed in, so the numeral is lodged inside the jumbled letters
typed badly means the letters of typed come out in the wrong order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A firm's poorly typed article, which a reporter filed as work.
explanation.walkthrough: TYPED reworked 'badly' gives PYEDT, with I placed inside to make PYEDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Correcting and preparing copy for publication is a task done in newspaper offices.

clue.text: Matchless woman in game

definitions.meaning: an unmarried older woman, without a partner, so unmatched
a children's card game in which the player left with the odd card loses

explanation.surface: A peerless woman taking part in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matchless' looks like unrivalled, but means without a match, a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dated term for an unmarried woman and the name of a children's card game.

clue.text: From the East, some of Asia's American Africans

indicators.note: From the East says the hidden letters are read backwards
some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A report about people of Asia and America from an eastern viewpoint, and about Africans.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania are a well-known East African ethnic group.

clue.text: Stripper beginning to strip before judge?

indicators.note: the first letter comes before the judge word
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a judge hears cases, so is one who hears

explanation.surface: A striptease artist starting to undress before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripper' looks like a dancer, but means someone who strips fleece from sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep farm worker removes the wool from the animals, so strips them.

clue.text: Blabbermouth talks with a government leader after uprising

indicators.note: uprising means going up, so in a down entry the letters are read upwards

parts.note: gabs means chatters or talks

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A chatterbox talks to a government leader after a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: GABSAG read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms are informal names for someone who talks too much.

clue.text: Principality with golden sun

parts.note: and means together with
or is the heraldic word for gold
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A small state blessed with golden sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny Pyrenean state is ruled by two co-princes, so it is formally a principality.

clue.text: Horse put up for review

indicators.note: put up means raised, so in a down entry the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a pacer is a horse trained to move with a lateral gait

explanation.surface: A horse offered for inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up for' looks like offering for sale; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A short summary going back over the main points, a noun for a brief restatement.

clue.text: Animal always going after stick — canine ultimately involved?

indicators.note: the always word is placed after the rest
involved means drawn inside, so that last letter goes into the stick word

parts.note: a rod is a stick

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the final letter of canine

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A dog forever chasing a stick, perhaps with a canine joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' suggests a dog is the animal, but only its last letter is used; E'ER is poetic for always.
explanation.definitionFit: This small European deer is a woodland mammal, so a beast of a specific kind.

clue.text: White knight in dark, invisible at the end

indicators.note: the last letter of the colour word disappears from view
the knight letter is put inside the colour word

parts.note: black is the colour of the dark
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess scene: the white knight placed among dark pieces, unseen by the end.
explanation.walkthrough: N inside BLACK makes BLANCK; dropping the last K gives the French word for white.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for the colour of snow, familiar from vin blanc.

clue.text: Intimate message is very good in revolutionary book

indicators.note: these letters go inside the reversed book name
revolutionary means turning round, so the book name is reversed

parts.note: Mark is a book of the New Testament
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A tender note says that a radical book is very fine.
explanation.walkthrough: MARK backwards is KRAM, which holds ISSOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting delivered with a kiss by a hired messenger is a message of an intimate kind.

clue.text: Try getting species into action and wish for success

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: the species abbreviation is put into the action word

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
sp is the abbreviation for species in biology

explanation.surface: An attempt to bring new species into play, while hoping it works.
explanation.definitionFit: An old blessing, said to someone setting out, hoping that their journey or venture prospers.

clue.text: Venture with fish shop

parts.note: to venture money is to bet it
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Taking a risk on a fish shop as a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' looks like a noun, but is the slang verb for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for reporting them to the police, an act of treachery.
